final_proof:
For a locale L, write O(L) for its frame of opens. A point of L, and hence an element of Sp(L), may be represented by a frame homomorphism p*: O(L) → 2, where 2 is the two-element frame.

For a ∈ O(L), define

U_a = {p ∈ Sp(L) : p*(a) = 1}.

These are the canonical basic opens of the spectrum. The component of the counit at L,

σ_L: ΩSp(L) → L,

is the locale morphism whose inverse-image frame homomorphism is

σ_L*: O(L) → O(Sp(L)),    a ↦ U_a.

This is a frame homomorphism: because every point p* preserves finite meets and arbitrary joins,

U_{a ∧ c} = U_a ∩ U_c    and    U_{∨ᵢ aᵢ} = ⋃ᵢ U_{aᵢ},

including the nullary cases.

Let f: L → M be any locale morphism, and let f*: O(M) → O(L) be its inverse-image frame homomorphism. The spectrum functor sends f to the continuous map

Sp(f): Sp(L) → Sp(M),    p* ↦ p* ∘ f*.

Consequently, for every b ∈ O(M),

Sp(f)⁻¹(U_b)
= {p : (p* ∘ f*)(b) = 1}
= {p : p*(f*(b)) = 1}
= U_{f*(b)}.                                      (1)

We compare the two locale morphisms from ΩSp(L) to M in the naturality square. Locale morphisms are equal exactly when their inverse-image frame homomorphisms are equal. For b ∈ O(M), the first composite satisfies

(f ∘ σ_L)*(b) = σ_L*(f*(b)) = U_{f*(b)}.

For the other composite, the inverse-image map of Ω(g) is the ordinary inverse-image map of the continuous map g. Hence, by (1),

(σ_M ∘ ΩSp(f))*(b)
= (ΩSp(f))*(σ_M*(b))
= Sp(f)⁻¹(U_b)
= U_{f*(b)}.

The two inverse-image frame homomorphisms therefore agree on every b ∈ O(M), so

f ∘ σ_L = σ_M ∘ ΩSp(f).

This holds for every locale morphism f: L → M, and it is precisely the naturality condition for σ: ΩSp ⇒ id_Loc. Thus the counit of the spectrum adjunction is a natural transformation.
